title: Finite projection-evaluation word and exact evaluation comparisons
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^{n+1}$, $n\in\mathbf N$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the ordinary module derived categories of the quotient sequence sites [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] and their signed closed tensor-Hom structures [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. For a compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow pY$ of $a$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and system model $m$ [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation], define a finite model at $n$ to consist of the actual quotient and integral point tensors, finite site tensor models, ordinary finite sections/proper-image/scalar-restriction lax tensors prescribed on local pure tensors, their universal derived adjunctions and strong tensor comparisons, sections pullback composition, and the canonical finite open tensor model [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model]. The finite tensor localizations agree with the recorded K-flat tensor comparison under the pure-tensor total-complex isomorphism. Define $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$, $h_n(U,N)=R\Gamma(X,R\mathcal Hom(U,N))$ with quotient action, and $b_n(U)=R\Gamma(Y,F_nU)$. Define $t_n$ by sections pullback composition followed by the sections counit, $v_n$ by $1\otimes t_n$, signed symmetry and closed evaluation, $\Pi_n$ by the proper counit-defined projection mate then the actual open tensor map and pullback compositor [def-exchange-projection], $q_n$ by sections projection then $\Pi_n$ and $F_n(v_n)$, and $\beta_n$ by scalar balancing then restricted signed symmetry and $q_n$. Scalar balancing is the scalar projection mate followed by $1\otimes$ the extension/restriction counit. Also define exact point evaluation, its restriction square, canonical native support evaluation, tensor-evaluation data normalized on all total complexes, and sections-evaluation data normalized by actual sections and universal right-derived units. This is data and specified formulas, with no assertion of existence.
